intent: Single-variable test: reduce mass from 0.5 to 0.4 kg (the allowed minimum) on the iteration-5 layout, to lower yaw inertia further and improve s-bend tracking. Expect s-bend max_error and progress to improve, oval finish rate to stay at 90% or higher, and slalom to be unchanged or slightly better.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Mass 0.4 kg lowers s-bend max_error below the 0.06 m limit and raises s-bend progress above 0.75 versus iteration 5. (2) Oval finish rate stays at or above 90%, since the radius-driven speed gain is unchanged. (3) If s-bend max_error stays at 0.06 m while line losses are low, the limit is turn authority, so the next step is wheel_track 0.09 m. (4) If slalom line_loss_events stay near 1.85, the limit is sensor coverage on alternating bends, so the next step is outer sensors at ±0.045 m with the same 16 mm footprint. (5) If steering_oscillation rises sharply while max_error does not move, the controller gain is the bottleneck and the Integrator should be told so.
rationale: Iteration 5 is the best design so far (422.9). Cutting mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg, with the iteration-4 layout otherwise unchanged, raised the oval finish rate from 80% to 95% and s-bend progress from 0.57 to 0.72. Mean s-bend max_error stayed at the 0.06 m off-track limit, so yaw inertia still limits the bends. The mass trend has been favourable at every step (0.8 to 0.6 kg did not hurt, and 0.6 to 0.5 kg helped), and the oval has margin, with mean finish time 1.71 s against the 3 s limit. Slalom is still the weak point: progress is 0.135 and line-loss events rose to 1.85, so the sensor coverage of the slalom's quick alternations is the bottleneck there, not mass alone. This iteration makes one change to keep the comparison clean: mass 0.5 to 0.4 kg, the lower bound. Sensors, wheel track (0.10 m) and wheel radius (0.040 m) stay fixed. Expected result: s-bend max_error and progress improve further (progress above 0.75), oval finish rate holds at 90% or better, and steering_oscillation does not rise sharply. If the s-bend stays at the 0.06 m limit with few line losses, the next lever is a narrower wheel_track (about 0.09 m) for more turn authority. If slalom line losses stay high, the next step is to widen the outer sensors to about ±0.045 m, which keeps tape visible to about 0.0655 m offset.
